title: Typing Blog: Speed, Accuracy and Keyboard Guides
description: Practical guides on typing speed, accuracy, average WPM by age and touch typing technique, written for anyone who wants faster and calmer hands.
lead: Long-form guides on speed, accuracy, technique and what the numbers actually mean. No gimmicks, just what works.

p: Every article is written for people who type for a living or are preparing for an exam, and each one ends with something you can practise the same day. We cover the mechanics of speed, the maths behind WPM, realistic benchmarks by age and profession, and the technique fixes that remove plateaus.

If you are brand new to touch typing, start with the beginner guide and work through the lessons alongside it. If you already type quickly and want to break a ceiling, the accuracy and speed articles will be more useful.

title: About KeyQuest: The Typing Test and Game Arcade
description: Learn who builds KeyQuest, why the site mixes serious typing tests with arcade games, and how WPM, accuracy and leaderboards are calculated here.
lead: KeyQuest is a free typing site built on one idea: practice only works if you come back tomorrow.

p: Typing is the one computer skill almost everybody uses every day and almost nobody trains. Most people learn by accident, settle somewhere around 40 words per minute and stay there for twenty years. The tools that could fix that are usually either clinical drill software that nobody opens twice, or games with no real measurement behind them.

KeyQuest is the middle path. Underneath it is a strict measurement engine: standard five character words, keystroke level accuracy, honest timing that starts on your first key. On top of it sits an arcade — ten games, three difficulty levels, a daily challenge and achievement badges — so that the practice is something you actually want to do.

Speed is always WPM = (correct characters / 5) / (seconds / 60), and accuracy is always ((keystrokes - errors) / keystrokes) x 100. We never count incorrect characters toward speed and we never hide errors you corrected, because the point of a measurement is to be useful rather than flattering.
Game scores multiply WPM by accuracy so that careful typing wins, and every result is stored against the game, the difficulty and the date, which is what makes the dashboard chart meaningful.

blocks.h2: What is free and what an account adds
ul: Free for everyone: all typing tests, all practice drills, the twelve touch typing lessons and all ten games.
With a free account: saved WPM history, per game statistics, achievement badges, daily challenge results and leaderboard placement.
No ads interrupt a test, and we never require payment to see your score.

p: KeyQuest is built and maintained by a small independent team of developers who got tired of their own typing plateaus. We read every message sent through the contact page, and a large share of the features on the site, including the daily challenge and the difficulty levels, came from user suggestions.

faqs.q: Is KeyQuest really free?
faqs.a: Yes. Every test, lesson and game is free and unlimited, and an account is optional. We do not charge for results or lock features behind a subscription.

faqs.q: Do you sell my typing data?
faqs.a: No. We store the minimum needed to show your history and leaderboards, and we never sell personal data. The privacy policy explains exactly what is kept.

faqs.q: Can I suggest a new game or feature?
faqs.a: Please do. Use the contact page; feature requests from users are the main source of our roadmap, including difficulty levels and the daily challenge.

faqs.q: Which keyboards and layouts are supported?
faqs.a: Any physical keyboard and any layout, including QWERTY, Dvorak, Colemak and Devanagari input methods for the Hindi test.

faqs.q: Do you have a mobile app?
faqs.a: Not yet. The site works in any modern browser, and we recommend a physical keyboard for a fair measurement of speed.

title: Contact KeyQuest: Support, Feedback and Bug Reports
description: Get in touch with the KeyQuest team about bugs, leaderboard issues, feature ideas, account problems or partnership enquiries. We reply within two days.
lead: Questions, bugs, leaderboard disputes or a game idea you cannot stop thinking about — send it over.

p: Email hello@keyquest.app and you will normally get a reply within two working days. There is one inbox and a real person reads it, so a short, specific message gets the fastest answer.
ul: Bug reports: tell us the page, your browser and keyboard layout, and what you expected to happen.
Account help: write from the email address on the account so we can verify it safely. Never send us your password.
Leaderboard reports: include the game, the difficulty and the player name; verified cheating is removed by our moderators.
Feature ideas: describe the practice problem you are trying to solve rather than the solution, and we will look for the simplest fix.
Press and partnerships: mention the audience and the format you have in mind.

p: A lot of questions are already answered on the about page, in the blog guides, or in the FAQ at the bottom of each test page. If your score did not save, check that you were signed in before the run finished, because results are attached to an account at the moment they are submitted.
If a game feels unresponsive, make sure the game area has focus by clicking it once, and check that your browser is not blocking the Web Audio sounds used for key feedback.

faqs.q: How quickly do you reply?
faqs.a: Within two working days for almost every message. Account recovery requests can take a little longer because we verify the email address on the account first.

faqs.q: My score did not save. What happened?
faqs.a: Scores are attached to your account when the run finishes, so a run started while signed out will not save. Sign in first, then play, and the result will appear in your dashboard history.

faqs.q: How do I report a suspected cheater?
faqs.a: Email us the game name, difficulty and the player name shown on the leaderboard. Our moderators can flag or remove individual results after review.

faqs.q: Can I delete my account and data?
faqs.a: Yes. Email us from the address on the account and we will delete the account, its results and its badges permanently.

faqs.q: Do you accept guest posts?
faqs.a: Occasionally, if the author genuinely knows the subject and the article is original. Send a short outline rather than a finished draft.

title: Privacy Policy: How KeyQuest Handles Your Data
description: Read how KeyQuest collects, stores and protects your data, which cookies we set, how analytics consent works and how to delete your account for good.
lead: Last updated June 2026. The short version: we store what is needed to show your typing history, and nothing is sold.

ul: Account data: your display name, email address, a securely hashed password and the date you registered. Passwords are hashed with bcrypt and are never stored or transmitted in readable form.
Result data: for each completed run, the game, difficulty, score, WPM, accuracy, duration and timestamp, plus whether it was a daily challenge.
Technical data: standard server logs, which include an IP address for abuse prevention and rate limiting on sign-in.
Analytics data: only if you accept analytics cookies. Analytics is loaded through Google Analytics 4 with anonymised page and event data.

p: KeyQuest sets an httpOnly authentication cookie and a refresh cookie when you sign in. These are strictly necessary for the site to keep you logged in and cannot be disabled while you are signed in.

Your browser's local storage holds non-identifying preferences: your theme choice, the sound mute toggle, your preferred difficulty and your cookie consent decision. Analytics cookies are only set after you choose Accept in the consent banner, and you can withdraw consent at any time by clearing site data.

Account and result data exists to run the features you asked for: your dashboard, your WPM chart, your achievement badges, the daily challenge board and the public leaderboards. Your display name is visible on leaderboards; your email address never is.

We do not sell personal data, we do not share it with advertisers, and we do not profile you for marketing. Aggregate, anonymised statistics may be used to write articles, for example average speeds across difficulty levels.

You can request a copy of your data or ask us to delete your account at any time by emailing hello@keyquest.app from the address on the account. Deletion removes your profile, results and badges permanently, and leaderboard entries disappear with them.
Children under 13 should use KeyQuest with a parent or guardian and should not create an account with a personal email address.

blocks.h2: Security and changes to this policy
p: Traffic is served over HTTPS, passwords are hashed with bcrypt, sign-in is rate limited after repeated failures and administrative pages require an admin role. No system is perfect, so please report any security concern to us directly.
If this policy changes we will update the date at the top of this page. Material changes will also be announced on the blog.

faqs.q: Do you use tracking cookies?
faqs.a: Only analytics cookies, and only after you accept them in the consent banner. Authentication cookies are strictly necessary and are set only when you sign in.

faqs.q: Can I use KeyQuest without an account?
faqs.a: Yes. All tests, lessons and games work signed out, and nothing is stored about you beyond standard server logs.

faqs.q: Where is my data stored?
faqs.a: In a managed MongoDB database used only by KeyQuest. Access is restricted to the application and to site administrators.

faqs.q: How do I delete my data?
faqs.a: Email hello@keyquest.app from your account address and we will permanently delete the account, its results and its achievement records.

faqs.q: Is my password readable by anyone?
faqs.a: No. Passwords are hashed with bcrypt before storage, so neither we nor an attacker with database access can read them.

title: Terms of Service: Rules for Using KeyQuest
description: The terms for using KeyQuest, covering accounts, fair play on leaderboards, acceptable use, intellectual property, liability and how disputes are handled.
lead: Last updated June 2026. Use the site, practise hard, do not cheat the leaderboard.

p: By using KeyQuest you agree to these terms. If you do not agree, please do not use the site. We may update the terms as the product changes, and the date above reflects the current version.

You are responsible for keeping your password safe and for everything done through your account. Give us an email address you control, choose a display name that is not offensive or impersonating someone else, and do not share logins. We may suspend accounts that break these rules or that are used to attack the service.
Sign-in attempts are rate limited to protect accounts, so repeated wrong passwords will temporarily lock sign-in for that email.

Leaderboards only mean something if the scores are real. Submitting results produced by scripts, macros, text expanders, modified clients or network tools is prohibited, and our moderators may flag or delete any result that is clearly not human typing. Repeated manipulation leads to account removal.
The daily challenge is validated on the server against the day's game and difficulty, so results submitted for the wrong combination are rejected automatically.

ul: Do not attempt to break, overload, scrape at scale, or gain unauthorised access to the service.
Do not use KeyQuest to store or transmit unlawful content, including in display names.
Do not resell access to the site or present it as your own product.
Automated access is allowed only for well-behaved search engine crawlers following robots.txt.

p: The KeyQuest name, interface, games, lesson material and articles are our intellectual property and may not be copied wholesale. You are welcome to quote an article with a link back, and to share your own result cards anywhere you like.
Typing passages include public domain and originally written text. If you believe something here infringes your rights, contact us and we will review it promptly.

KeyQuest is provided as is, without warranty. We aim for high availability but we cannot guarantee uninterrupted service, preserved scores in the event of a failure, or that measurements match any particular exam's official scoring. To the extent permitted by law, our liability is limited to the amount you paid us, which for a free service is zero.
These terms are governed by the laws applicable at our principal place of business, and disputes will be handled in those courts.

faqs.q: Can I use KeyQuest results in a job application?
faqs.a: Yes, and we recommend quoting a three or five minute result. KeyQuest is not an accredited certification body, so some employers will still run their own assessment.

faqs.q: What counts as cheating?
faqs.a: Any result not produced by you typing on a keyboard in real time: scripts, macros, text expanders, autocomplete tools or modified clients. Moderators can flag or remove such results.

faqs.q: Can my account be deleted without warning?
faqs.a: Only for serious abuse, such as attacking the service or repeated leaderboard manipulation. In other cases we contact you first using the email on the account.

faqs.q: May I embed KeyQuest tests on my site?
faqs.a: Not without written permission, but you are very welcome to link to any page, and links to specific tests are encouraged.

faqs.q: Do these terms change?
faqs.a: Occasionally, as features change. The updated date at the top of this page always reflects the current version, and significant changes are announced on the blog.
